title: Harness incrementality measurement for CTV success | Adjust

facts.fact: Per a martech.org source cited by Adjust, CTV advertising is expected to grow by 13.2% globally (third-party projection, as reported on the Adjust page).
Per Adjust's citation, CTV is expected to hit US$25.9 billion by the end of 2023.
facts.quote: hit US$25.9 billion by the end of 2023

facts.fact: Adjust states that incrementality tests split a target audience into a control group that does not see the CTV ad and a test group exposed to the ad, then compare effectiveness.
facts.quote: split a target audience into a control group that doesn’t see the CTV ad at all and a test group that is exposed to the ad, comparing for effectiveness

facts.fact: Adjust describes three CTV incrementality methods: geo-testing, PSA testing, and predictive modeling, with geo-testing and PSA testing both requiring significant upfront investment.
facts.quote: The three main methods to measure incrementality on CTV

facts.fact: Adjust states that predictive modeling uses synthetic control groups with variables matching the test group, such as user behavior and demographics.
facts.quote: synthetic control groups, which have matching variables to the test group, such as user behavior, demographics, and other factors

facts.fact: Adjust states that most CTV devices do not currently offer clickable ad campaigns, although this is starting to change.
facts.quote: most CTV devices do not currently offer clickable ad campaigns (although this is starting to change)
